name: Idaho

creditorClaims.text: A published notice requires claims within 4 months after first publication; creditors given written notice have the later of that period or 60 days after mailing (Idaho Code § 15-3-801); pre-death claims are barred at the earlier of 3 years after death or those periods (Idaho Code § 15-3-803).

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, an estate may be closed by verified statement no earlier than 6 months after original appointment, after the claims period has expired (Idaho Code § 15-3-1003).

smallEstate.text: Thirty days after death, successors may collect property by affidavit if the fair market value of the probate estate, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $100,000 and no personal representative or summary administration is pending or granted (Idaho Code § 15-3-1201). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Affidavit collection up to $100,000 (Idaho Code § 15-3-1201); summary administration and informal probate under Idaho Code title 15, chapter 3.

filingFee.text: District court probate filing fees are set in Idaho Code title 31, chapter 32; the probate-specific amount was not located in § 31-3201 as read.

personalRepFee.text: A personal representative is entitled to reasonable compensation for services (Idaho Code § 15-3-719).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule; attorney compensation is reviewable for reasonableness (Idaho Code § 15-3-721, UPC equivalent, not read).
